question: If 2 times a son's age is added to his father's age, the sum is 46 years. If 2.5 times the father's age is added to the son's age, the sum is 97 years. What is the father's age (in years)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiply the second given condition by 2 to equate the son's age multipliers.

New Condition 2: 5 × Father + 2 × Son = 194

Condition 1: 1 × Father + 2 × Son = 46

Subtract Condition 1 from New Condition 2: 4 × Father = 148 ⇒ Father = 37

**∴ The correct answer is 37 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Father's age = F, Son's age = S

⇒ F + 2S = 46 ... (i)

⇒ 2.5F + S = 97 ... (ii)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Multiply equation (ii) by 2:

⇒ 5F + 2S = 194 ... (iii)

⇒ Subtract equation (i) from equation (iii):

⇒ (5F + 2S) − (F + 2S) = 194 − 46

⇒ 4F = 148

⇒ F = 148 ÷ 4

⇒ F = 37

**∴ The correct answer is 37 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

When two different conditions are provided for two unknowns, they form a system of linear equations which can be solved simultaneously to find both variables.

Elimination Method

Multiply the equations by appropriate constants to equalise the coefficient of one variable, then subtract one equation from the other to easily find the value of the second variable.
